issues.legal_issue: A manufacturing-purpose tenancy that is not from year to year does not require six months’ notice for termination and may be terminated by the notice applicable to other than year-to-year tenancies.
material_facts: The tenancy was found to be from month to month and not from year to year or for a term exceeding one year.
The tenancy was for a manufacturing purpose.
The written document recording the tenancy was unregistered, and the court held that its terms could not be relied upon.
A notice giving 30 days to quit was served, and the tenant did not comply.
The High Court held that six months’ notice was required and dismissed the ejectment suit; the Supreme Court reversed that decision.
issues.conclusion: The 30-day notice was valid. The appeal was allowed and the first appellate court’s order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, absent a contract to the contrary, a manufacturing-purpose lease is deemed to be from year to year and terminable by six months’ notice only where it is from year to year. A lease that is not from year to year falls under the provision for other tenancies and is terminable by 15 days’ notice. Section 107 requires a registered instrument for a lease from year to year or for a term exceeding one year; the unregistered document could not be relied upon, but the undisputed month-to-month tenancy did not attract that requirement. No earlier cases were relied upon.

rule.if: ejectment_proceeding and manufacturing_purpose and not year_to_year_or_long_term_lease and notice_gave_at_least_fifteen_days

predicates.ejectment_proceeding: The landlord brought a proceeding seeking to terminate the tenancy and recover possession.
predicates.manufacturing_purpose: The premises were leased for a manufacturing purpose.
predicates.year_to_year_or_long_term_lease: The tenancy was from year to year or was for a term exceeding one year.
predicates.notice_gave_at_least_fifteen_days: The landlord gave the tenant at least 15 days’ notice to quit.

issues.definition: When an ejectment proceeding concerns a manufacturing-purpose tenancy that is not from year to year or for a term exceeding one year, a notice of at least 15 days makes the termination notice valid.
